field_updates.detail: p1 'Permissible film temperature, ϑF max. 155 °C'; p1 'The rated dissipation applies only if the permitted film temperature is not exceeded'; P70 (standard) for CRCW0603 = 0.1 W (p2); p6 Derating figure: CRCW0603 line flat at 0.1 W to 70 °C, reaching 0 W at 155 °C (visually read). Method: Rth = (155 - 70) K / 0.1 W = 850.0 K/W. Linear derating means film/element temperature = T_amb + Rth*P reaches the endpoint on the derating line, so Rth_implied = (T_end - T_knee)/P_rated. This is the derating-implied thermal resistance on the manufacturer's (unstated) reference mounting, not a measured or board-specific value. Caveat: the same part's extended-operation rating (p2: 0.125 W at 70 °C, p6 extended derating also to 0 at 155 °C) implies 680.0 K/W, so the derating-implied Rth is a rating construct that depends on the operation mode, not a physical package constant.
